what: BioNTech is a German biotechnology company. It co-developed the first widely used COVID-19 vaccine with Pfizer, and is now spending that money on cancer immunotherapy, including mRNA cancer vaccines and antibodies.
customers: Governments and health systems buying vaccines; future cancer medicines would be sold to oncologists and health systems.
money: cancer immunotherapy programmes and partnership payments
moat: mRNA manufacturing and clinical experience proven at enormous scale, plus intellectual property and partnerships with large pharmaceutical companies.
risks: Vaccine revenue has collapsed from its peak and keeps falling
It makes a large operating loss while funding cancer research
Cancer trials are long and most programmes fail
Revenue has fallen about 43% a year over three years
opportunities: Cash of about $16 billion against almost no debt, an unusual war chest
A partnership with Bristol Myers Squibb on a bispecific cancer antibody brought large upfront payments
Analysts see about 36% upside from current levels
watch: Late-stage cancer trial readouts and the cash burn rate.
